standouts.name: Pocket Flights: scan-to-phone live flight platform, no app
standouts.why: QR codes in terminals and at gates open a mobile web flight tool, removing the install barrier and giving the airport a shell for adding journey services. Evidence level: search.

standouts.name: Smart Gates Eligibility PreCheck (July 2026, with GDRFA)
standouts.why: A phone-camera scan of the passport photo page returns an instant answer on biometric gate eligibility before the passenger queues, turning opaque immigration rules into a ten-second self-service. Evidence level: search.

standouts.name: DXB Express Maps from every flight information screen
standouts.why: The QR on the screen gives a known start point and opens wayfinding to gates, dining, shops, lounges, toilets and service desks; launched for a peak period alongside marked accessible routes. Evidence level: search.

standouts.name: DXB for All accessibility programme
standouts.why: Sunflower lanyards (36,040 by end of 2025), autism-friendly route, hearing loops at 520+ touchpoints, Assisted Travel Lounge, visual Travel Planner and a public pledge to be the most accessible airport by 2035. Evidence level: search (self-reported).

standouts.name: Always-on omnichannel contact (phone, WhatsApp, live chat, AI chatbot)
standouts.why: One contact page lists all channels, backed by an outsourced always-on centre and a vendor-reported AI chatbot; the same channels served as the official route during a March 2026 surge. Evidence level: search.

weaknesses: Website is bilingual only (English and Arabic) despite a highly international passenger base and 25-language terminal announcements [search] https://dubaiairports.ae/

Fragmented estate and identity: separate hosts and registrations for DXB, DWC, Al Majlis (forced re-registration April 2025), Pocket Flights, DXBmore.com and operator checkouts; no single account or basket evidenced [search] https://servicesedge.dubaiairports.ae/MajlisBooking

No personalisation layer and no official app: no accounts, saved flights or loyalty evidenced; myDXB reportedly removed and unofficial apps fill the stores [search, forum] https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowTopic-g1-i10702-k15312848-Dubai_Airport_App-Air_Travel.html
Thin transit tooling: procedural transfer text, no minimum connection times or connection planner, manual DXB-DWC transfer [search] https://dubaiairports.ae/information/transfers

Opaque AI assistant and weak web hygiene: chatbot documented only by its vendor; legacy 404 and dev/authoring hosts indexed; no site accessibility statement found [search] https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=fpmZCTSsL_Q
ideas: One scan, one journey: a single progressive web app opened by QR from flight screens, totems and boarding-pass emails, pre-filtered to the passenger's flight with live status, walking time from the scan point, queue estimates, transfer steps and a built-in disruption mode (Dubai splits this across three tools).

Genuinely multilingual with a transparent assistant: full Bahasa Malaysia and English editions plus human-reviewed core journeys in key inbound languages, honest labelling of machine-translated pages, and one named assistant with published scope, languages and human handover (Dubai offers two site languages and no official chatbot documentation).
Immigration lane and autogate eligibility checker that needs no passport scan: nationality, pass type and age band in, correct lane and required pre-arrival forms out, usable before travel.
A real connection planner: published terminal-to-terminal times, minimum connection guidance by ticket type and a will-I-make-it answer for a pair of flights.
Single account and single basket for parking, fast track, lounge, meet-and-greet, food order-to-gate and reserve-and-collect, with guest checkout first and optional loyalty.
Accessibility as a product feature: WCAG 2.2 AA statement, step-free and low-sensory map routing, online assistance and sunflower lanyard requests, visual journey planner in every language.
